themes_detail.label: Street Sign Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street signs are disappearing and being damaged at crisis levels this week on the Upper East Side: 8 damaged signs THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (611% spike, z-score 5.9) plus 6 missing signs last week vs. 1.1 weekly average (433% spike, z-score 4.63), suggesting systematic infrastructure failure or theft that requires immediate DOT investigation.
evidence: 8 street sign damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (611% increase, z-score 5.9)
6 street sign missing complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (433% increase, z-score 4.63)
Combined 14 sign-related complaints in past 2 weeks vs. ~2.2 typical weekly volume indicates acute problem
reporting_angles: Contact DOT to determine if this is vandalism, theft, or maintenance backlog; request photos and complaint locations
Interview residents on affected streets about safety implications (obscured stop signs, directional confusion)

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints spiked to 4 reports THIS WEEK compared to a 0.5 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 4.95), suggesting a potential contamination event or system failure affecting Upper East Side tap water that demands urgent DEP and health department verification.
evidence: 4 water quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 4.95)
Spike is recent and acute—no sustained baseline complaints in prior 8 weeks
Issue directly affects resident health and daily life across the district
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP immediately for water system alerts, testing results, or known main breaks in UES
Interview affected residents on specific complaints (discoloration, odor, taste) and get exact addresses to map cluster

themes_detail.label: Helicopter Noise Crisis (3 weeks old)
themes_detail.summary: Helicopter noise complaints exploded to 11 reports 3 weeks ago vs. a 0.1 weekly average (8700% spike, z-score 32.88)—the most statistically extreme anomaly in the dataset—suggesting a new flight pattern, emergency, or special event that may be ongoing or recurring.
evidence: 11 helicopter noise complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (8700% increase, z-score 32.88—highest severity in dataset)
Massive statistical anomaly indicates sudden, unusual activity rather than normal baseline
If pattern is recurring, could affect hundreds of residents daily
reporting_angles: Check FAA records and NYC Police/Emergency Services logs for 3 weeks ago—was there an emergency response, special operation, or VIP movement?
Interview residents on when the noise occurred and whether it has continued; determine if it's a one-time event or new pattern

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Surge
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 26 reports 2 weeks ago vs. a 9.4 weekly average (177% spike, z-score 5.71), indicating accelerating pedestrian safety hazards across the district that may reflect deferred maintenance or weather damage.
evidence: 26 sidewalk condition complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 9.4 weekly baseline (177% increase, z-score 5.71)
Affects pedestrian safety across multiple blocks; elderly residents on UES particularly vulnerable
May correlate with recent weather (freeze-thaw cycles) or indicate chronic DOT maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Map the 26 complaints to identify geographic clusters (specific blocks or intersections); contact DOT for repair timelines
Interview elderly residents and mobility-limited pedestrians about trip hazards; include photos of worst sidewalk sections

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints surged to 11 reports last week vs. a 2.1 weekly average (418% spike, z-score 4.84), suggesting either rapid expansion of dining sheds, unresolved quality-of-life conflicts with residents, or enforcement gaps as the district navigates post-pandemic outdoor seating.
evidence: 11 outdoor dining complaints last week vs. 2.1 weekly baseline (418% spike, z-score 4.84)
Spike is recent and acute, indicating either new expansion or emerging resident friction
Issue reflects broader city policy questions around permanent outdoor seating post-pandemic
reporting_angles: Map the 11 complaints to see if they cluster on specific avenues (e.g., Madison Ave, Lexington Ave); contact SBS for dining shed permits issued recently
Interview restaurant owners and nearby residents about specific grievances (noise, waste, accessibility, space encroachment)
